title: Submission metadata can be linked to a specific student across courses and over time
description: The flow carries direct identifiers (student id) together with course, submission timestamp, login context, and assignment file. This enables the portal to link multiple submissions and activity events to the same student, potentially building a longitudinal profile of study behavior and performance-related activity.
assumptions: The web app stores or can observe these fields together per submission/session.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgment because the retrieved context gives threat-type applicability but not the detailed subtree for linkability.

title: Student identity is disclosed to the portal through direct identifiers in the upload flow
description: The flow includes the student id and authenticated login interaction, revealing the student's identity to the receiving process. If identity is exposed more broadly within the application than necessary, this creates identifiability risk.
assumptions: The student id is unique and directly identifies the student within the institution.
uncertainty_note: Direct identifiability clearly applies; tree node is approximate.

title: Insufficient submission evidence could let the portal deny or contest a student's submission
description: If the system does not generate trustworthy proof of receipt for the uploaded assignment, the receiving process may later dispute that a specific student submitted a particular file at a specific time. This creates a privacy-relevant non-repudiation gap around the student's action history.
assumptions: No strong receipt, timestamped acknowledgment, or tamper-evident audit trail is guaranteed by the current flow description.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the portal already issues verifiable submission receipts; not stated in the flow description.

title: Assignment content and submission metadata may be detectable in transit or by intermediaries
description: The uploaded work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp may be observable from network traffic, logs, or intermediaries if transport protection and logging minimization are inadequate. Even when content is encrypted, traffic patterns may still reveal that a student submitted coursework at a particular time.
assumptions: Potential observers include network intermediaries, reverse proxies, or internal logging components.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability depends on transport security and operational logging controls, which are not described.

title: Excessive collection of submission metadata may reveal sensitive personal or behavioral information
description: The combination of assignment file, student id, course, and precise submission timestamp can reveal study habits, deadlines missed, time-zone/location patterns, disability-related accommodations, or other sensitive inferences from the student's academic behavior.
assumptions: The system retains precise timestamps and associates them with identifiable student records.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure of information applies strongly; specific downstream sensitive inferences may vary by context.

title: Student may be unaware of how submission data and metadata are processed
description: From this flow alone, the student may not understand what data are collected on upload, how long the file and metadata are retained, who can access them, whether they are used for plagiarism detection or analytics, or whether submission timestamps are visible to instructors and administrators.
assumptions: The interface may not provide clear, timely privacy notices or just-in-time explanations at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness depends on the portal's notices and UX, which are not described.

title: Assignment submission may process more personal data than necessary or without an appropriate legal basis/notice
description: If the portal collects or retains the full assignment file, direct student identifier, course association, and precise timestamp beyond what is necessary for assessment and records management, the flow may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or transparency obligations.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements mandate minimization, defined retention, and transparent notice for educational systems.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance is context-dependent on jurisdiction, institutional policy, and implemented controls; tree node is approximate.

title: Student identifier is forwarded to the grading service
description: The flow includes student id together with course, file reference, and requesting role. This directly identifies the student to the Assignment & Grading Service, enabling processing of identified submissions and grading requests.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier within the institution and is not irreversibly pseudonymised before transmission.

title: Grading service processes identified submission/grading requests
description: Because the portal routes submission and grading requests containing a student id, the receiving service processes identified data rather than anonymous data. This creates an identifying privacy threat at the receiver if identification is not strictly necessary for each processing step.
assumptions: The receiving service can associate the student id with a specific individual or account.

title: Submission and grading requests may become attributable evidence of student actions
description: A routed request containing student id, course, file reference, and requesting role can serve as evidence that a particular student submitted work or initiated a grading-related action for a course. If logged or retained by the grading service, this may prevent the student from plausibly denying involvement in that action.
assumptions: The service logs or stores request metadata with sufficient integrity and retention to be used as evidence later.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include the specific Non-repudiation subtree.

title: Student activity becomes detectable by the grading service
description: This flow reveals that a specific student is interacting with a specific course context and has an associated submission/grading event. Even without inspecting file contents, the metadata makes the student's academic activity detectable to the receiving service or anyone observing it there.
assumptions: The grading service or its operators can observe request metadata such as student id, course, and timing.
uncertainty_note: Specific detectability subtree citation is approximate; exact node may differ in the full LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Role and course metadata may allow profiling beyond the user's expectations
description: The combination of requesting role, course, file reference, and student id can reveal the nature of the user's interaction with the academic system. If the portal does not make this onward sharing clear, users may be unaware that the grading service receives enough context to infer submission status and academic participation.
assumptions: Users primarily interact with the portal and may not understand which downstream services receive their metadata.
uncertainty_note: Specific unawareness tree node is based on best judgement; retrieved context did not include the U subtree.

title: Forwarding identified grading data may exceed user expectations or declared purpose
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to another process. If the data sharing, purpose, or role-based use is not properly communicated or lacks an appropriate legal basis, the flow can create a non-compliance risk with transparency, purpose limitation, or data minimisation obligations.
assumptions: Applicable policy or regulatory requirements require clear notice, necessity, and minimisation for this inter-process sharing.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-compliance subtree citation is approximate because the retrieved context did not include the Nc subtree.

title: Excessive storage of submission metadata with assignment content
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment file together with student id, course, and precise submission time. For this flow, a privacy threat exists if all of these attributes are retained in the store when some are not strictly necessary for grading or later academic handling. Storing identifying data and detailed timestamps alongside the file can constitute avoidable explicit disclosure within the system and increases exposure if the store is later accessed for other purposes.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 retains the full file and associated metadata as part of persistent storage, and that at least some metadata granularity or retention may exceed what is strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->DataStore but does not provide the exact subtree id for this case.

title: Stored assignment records enable identification of the student
description: This flow persists the assignment together with a student identifier and course information in the data store. The combination directly identifies, or makes easily identifiable, the submitting student for each stored assignment record. If direct identification is not necessary at storage level, this creates an identifiability threat because the store contains plainly attributable records rather than less identifying references or separated identity data.
assumptions: Assumes student id is a direct identifier or can readily be mapped to a student by components with access to DS1.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; applicability of Identifiability is strong because the stored tuple explicitly includes student id.

title: Submission records can be linked across coursework and time
description: Because the stored data includes student id, course, submission time, and assignment content, records in DS1 can be linked to one another to reconstruct a student's submission history across tasks or courses. Even where each item is legitimate on its own, their joint storage in a persistent repository creates a linkability threat by enabling correlation of multiple actions to the same student.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores multiple submissions over time and permits querying or analysis across records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; retrieved context establishes L is applicable for Process->DataStore, but not the specific node.

title: Stored metadata allows inference of student behavior and circumstances
description: Precise submission timestamps, course association, and assignment content may allow observers of DS1 to infer behavioral patterns such as lateness, working habits, enrollment, academic difficulties, or special circumstances. Even without additional data flows, the metadata persisted by this flow can reveal more about the student than the primary grading purpose requires, creating a detectability threat through observability of submission events and patterns.
assumptions: Assumes entities with access to DS1 can inspect stored records or metadata and compare submissions over time.
uncertainty_note: This is a moderate-confidence detectability/inference concern; some methodologies might classify parts of this scenario under disclosure or linkability instead.

title: Storage may exceed purpose limitation or lawful basis expectations
description: The flow stores the submitted file with student id, course, and submission time. A non-compliance threat exists if the system stores more personal data than declared, retains it longer than necessary, or uses the stored submission package for secondary purposes beyond grading and academic administration without an appropriate legal basis or transparency. The risk is located at the data store because persistent retention is what makes such policy or regulatory deviation material.
assumptions: Assumes applicable education/privacy rules require purpose limitation, data minimization, retention limits, and transparency for student submission data.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; compliance assessment depends on the actual retention policy, notices, and legal basis, which are not provided.

title: Portal processes identified teacher account data during login
description: To authenticate the teacher and return the correct review queue, the web app processes directly identifying account data and course association information. This can create an identifying privacy threat if more identity attributes than necessary are collected, retained, or exposed during the login/request flow.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes teacher username, institutional account identifier, or equivalent directly identifying credentials tied to course assignments.

title: Teacher role and course assignments may be disclosed beyond necessity
description: The request for the submissions queue reveals that the requester is a teacher and is associated with particular courses. If the flow or its handling exposes these role/course relationships to unauthorized parties, it could disclose personal information about the teacher's professional assignments.
assumptions: Assumes the request or resulting session context contains course identifiers and teacher-role information.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not provide a more specific disclosure node.

title: Teacher may be unaware of profiling based on review-queue access patterns
description: By processing requests for submission-review queues, the portal can infer workload, teaching activity, and course engagement patterns of a teacher. If this inference and any subsequent use are not transparent, the teacher may be unaware of how their activity data is being used.
assumptions: Assumes access requests are logged or analyzed for operational, monitoring, or analytics purposes.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the system logs or analyzes teacher access behavior; exact threat-tree node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Login and queue-request processing may exceed the teacher's reasonable expectations
description: If the portal uses the login and queue-request data for secondary purposes such as analytics, performance monitoring, or sharing with other systems without an appropriate legal basis or clear notice, the processing may be non-compliant with data protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes possible secondary use, retention, or sharing of login/request metadata beyond strict service delivery.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance-oriented threat contingent on actual governance and notice practices, which are not specified in the flow description.

title: Exposure of identifiable student submissions to an unintended teacher account
description: The portal displays student names, work content, and submission times to a teacher. If authorization or session handling is flawed, the data flow could disclose personal data and educational records to a teacher who is not permitted to view that student's submissions.
assumptions: Assumes teacher access is role-based and should be limited to classes/courses they teach.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure on a process-to-external-entity flow; retrieved context confirms D applies to this interaction but does not provide the exact subtree citation.

title: Student activity can be linked across submissions and timestamps
description: Because the portal presents student names together with work content and submission times, the teacher can readily link multiple submissions and activity events to the same identifiable student, enabling profiling of participation, habits, and performance over time beyond what may be necessary for the immediate task.
assumptions: Assumes the interface exposes historical or repeated submission events in a way that supports correlation.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is inherent in showing direct identifiers with multiple events, though some linking may be necessary for grading; risk depends on data minimization and UI design.

title: Student identity is identifiable from displayed submission data
description: The flow explicitly includes student names alongside submitted work and timestamps, making the student directly identifiable to the recipient. If anonymous or pseudonymous review is expected for some assessments, this display defeats that protection.
assumptions: Assumes some contexts may require blinded marking or reduced identity exposure.
uncertainty_note: Identifiability is certain from the described fields; whether it is a privacy threat depends on whether direct identification is necessary in this use case.

title: Displayed submission data may exceed what teachers were informed or authorized to receive
description: Showing full work content, names, and precise submission times may be incompatible with privacy notices, school policy, or purpose limitations if teachers only need a subset of this information for assessment. Excessive detail in the flow could therefore violate consent, expectation, or policy constraints.
assumptions: Assumes applicable school policy, privacy notice, or legal basis limits teacher-visible fields to what is necessary for grading/feedback.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends heavily on the institution's stated purpose, notices, and legal/policy basis, which were not provided.

title: Students may be unaware that exact submission times and full content are visible to teachers via the portal
description: If the system does not clearly communicate which submission metadata and content are shown to teachers, students may be unable to understand the privacy consequences of uploading work, undermining predictability and informed expectation.
assumptions: Assumes the portal or related notices do not clearly explain teacher visibility of submitted data and metadata.
uncertainty_note: This is plausible for educational portals generally, but the actual presence or absence of transparency notices is unknown.

title: Teacher identity can be inferred from grader ID in submitted grade record
description: The flow includes a grader ID together with student ID, grade, and written feedback. Anyone able to observe or access this transmission can identify which specific teacher evaluated which student work, revealing the teacher's involvement in a particular assessment event.
assumptions: Assumes grader ID is directly identifying or easily resolvable to a specific teacher, and that the flow may be accessible beyond strictly authorized components.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only confirms applicable threat types, not detailed node ids.

title: Sensitive academic evaluation data may be disclosed in transit to the web app
description: The teacher sends grade, feedback text, student ID, and grader ID to the portal. If the flow lacks adequate transport protection or is exposed through logs, browser instrumentation, intermediaries, or monitoring systems, confidential assessment information about the student and teacher may be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the transmission path or surrounding components could expose request contents, metadata, or application logs.
uncertainty_note: Detailed node id is approximate; disclosure in transit is clearly applicable but exact subtree labeling may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Teacher may later deny having submitted a specific grade or feedback entry
description: If the system does not create reliable evidence binding the authenticated teacher, submission time, assignment context, and exact content submitted, the teacher could repudiate having entered or approved the grade and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient audit logging, weak session binding, or lack of tamper-evident submission records.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation issues are common for grade submission flows, but exact node id is estimated.

title: Teacher may be unaware of secondary uses or visibility of submitted feedback
description: When recording grades and written feedback, the teacher may not understand who can later access the feedback, how long it is retained, whether it is reused for analytics or appeals, or whether comments become visible to students immediately. This creates a privacy unawareness risk around the processing of both teacher-linked and student-linked data.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly communicate downstream recipients, retention, publication timing, or reuse purposes.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on UI transparency and policy notices, which are not described in the flow.

title: Grade and feedback collection may exceed what is necessary or lack a clear legal basis
description: This flow collects student ID, grader ID, grade, and free-text feedback. The free-text field can capture excessive personal data, special-category data, or comments unrelated to grading, and the processing must also be justified and limited to explicit educational purposes. If the portal collects or retains more than necessary, or uses the data beyond the grading purpose, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes privacy requirements include purpose limitation, data minimization, and lawful processing obligations.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine compliance risk, but whether it materializes depends on institutional policy, configured retention, and controls on feedback content.

title: Grade records in the database directly identify students and graders
description: The written grade record contains student id and grader id alongside course, grade, feedback, and timestamp. Storing these direct identifiers in the grade records database makes the data attributable to specific student and staff members and increases identifiability if the datastore is accessed beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: DS2 stores the fields as described in the flow and they are retrievable together as one record.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement because the retrieved context only confirms applicable threat types for Process->DataStore, not detailed node ids.

title: Stored grade records reveal sensitive academic performance and assessment details
description: The database stores grade, feedback, course, and timestamp linked to a student. This can disclose personal academic performance, instructor assessments, and potentially special-category inferences from feedback content if the datastore is improperly accessed or reused.
assumptions: Free-text feedback may contain personal or sensitive remarks beyond the numeric/textual grade itself.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate best-judgement.

title: Persisted grader identity and timestamp create evidence that may be used for non-repudiation beyond necessity
description: By storing grader id and timestamp with each grade record, the system creates durable evidence tying a specific grader to an assessment event. While this may support accountability, it also introduces a privacy threat if such evidence is retained or used more broadly than necessary, limiting plausible deniability for staff actions.
assumptions: Grader id is a personal identifier for an individual staff member rather than a role or team account.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the design intends strong accountability; if this is strictly required by policy, the privacy concern is reduced but still relevant under LINDDUN.

title: Unclear retention or downstream use of grade records may leave students and graders insufficiently informed
description: This flow writes a rich grade record to persistent storage, but the flow description gives no indication that students and graders are informed about retention, access, reuse, or secondary processing of identifiers, grades, and feedback. Lack of transparency around this storage operation is a privacy threat.
assumptions: Notice about grading-data storage, retention, and access is not otherwise established outside this flow.
uncertainty_note: This threat is inferred from missing transparency information in the model rather than explicit evidence.

title: Persistent storage of identifiable grade records may exceed data-minimization or purpose-limitation requirements
description: The flow stores student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp together. Depending on legal basis and institutional policy, storing all these attributes in one persistent record may be more data than necessary for the primary purpose of recording grades, especially detailed feedback, exact timestamps, or direct grader identifiers.
assumptions: Not every stored field is strictly necessary in raw identifiable form for the long-term grade-record purpose.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on applicable education/privacy regulation and internal retention policies.

title: Portal request processing uses identified student data
description: To return the requesting student's grades and feedback, the web app must process identifiers that tie the request to a specific student account. This creates an identifying threat if more identifying data than necessary is collected, exposed in the request, or used beyond what is needed to fulfill the grades query.
assumptions: The student is authenticated or otherwise identified to the portal when making the request.

title: Request for grades reveals sensitive academic interest and status
description: A request for grades and feedback can disclose personal academic information about the student, including which course results or feedback are being accessed and potentially their academic status. If request contents, parameters, logs, or surrounding metadata are exposed, the student's personal data may be disclosed.
assumptions: The request or associated metadata may be logged, monitored, or visible to components beyond strict need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgment because the retrieved context did not provide a more specific disclosure node.

title: Insufficient proof of student request handling
description: If the portal does not create adequate, privacy-respecting evidence of the student's grades request and the system's response, either party may later be unable to demonstrate whether a request was made or fulfilled. This can create accountability gaps around access to sensitive educational records.
assumptions: The system may need auditable evidence of access requests to educational records.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-repudiation node id is an approximate best-fit because no Nr nodes were provided in the retrieved context.

title: Student may be unaware of request logging or secondary use
description: When requesting grades and feedback, the student may not be sufficiently informed that the portal logs access events, analyzes usage, or shares request metadata with supporting services. Lack of transparency undermines the student's ability to understand how their educational data is handled.
assumptions: The portal presents limited or unclear privacy information at the point of request.
uncertainty_note: Specific unawareness node id is an approximate best-fit because no U nodes were provided in the retrieved context.

title: Grades request may exceed purpose limitation or data minimization expectations
description: The flow may be non-compliant if the portal requests or retains more student data than necessary to deliver grades and feedback, or if the request data is later reused for analytics, monitoring, or other purposes incompatible with the original educational purpose.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy requirements impose purpose limitation, data minimization, and retention constraints.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-compliance node id is an approximate best-fit because no Nc nodes were provided in the retrieved context.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades or feedback to someone other than the student
description: The portal flow returns highly sensitive educational records and teacher feedback to an external entity. If authentication, session binding, access control, or recipient verification are weak, the data could be shown to the wrong person, exposing the student's academic information.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal is accessed over a user session and the system must ensure only the data subject can view their own records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement because the retrieved context only confirms that Identifiability/Information disclosure applies to Process→ExternalEntity flows, not the exact subtree id.

title: Exposure of special-category or sensitive personal data in the response
description: Grades and narrative teacher feedback can reveal sensitive personal data, such as learning difficulties, disciplinary issues, or inferred performance characteristics. Delivering this content to the student device may expose more personal data than necessary, especially through previews, shared devices, browser caches, or notifications.
assumptions: Assumes teacher feedback may contain sensitive or intimate educational observations and the student's device or environment may not be private.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subtree id may differ; selected as best judgement for data disclosure on a flow.

title: Excessive or unclear feedback presentation prevents the student from understanding privacy implications
description: If the portal displays grades, comments, metadata, or historical records without clear separation or explanation, the student may not understand what personal data is being presented, why it is shown, or who else may have access to it. This undermines user awareness and informed handling of their educational data.
assumptions: Assumes the portal UI may include contextual metadata or retained records beyond the immediate grade result.
uncertainty_note: Usability-related privacy threats are plausible on this display flow, but applicability depends on the actual UI design.

title: Displaying more educational data than necessary may violate data-minimization or purpose-limitation requirements
description: The flow's purpose is to show the student's own grades and feedback. If the portal also returns unrelated course history, internal staff notes, class comparisons, or other students' information, the disclosure would exceed the intended purpose and may conflict with education-privacy and data-protection obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to privacy requirements such as educational-record confidentiality and general data-protection principles.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance risk depends on jurisdiction and exact fields included in the response.

title: Lack of auditable evidence of grade/feedback disclosure to the student
description: If the system does not log when grades and feedback were displayed, to which authenticated account, and under what session, it may be impossible to demonstrate whether the educational data was disclosed correctly or to investigate privacy incidents involving improper access.
assumptions: Assumes auditability of educational-record access is required for incident handling or accountability.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability can vary in LINDDUN usage for read-only viewing flows, but accountability concerns are genuine here.

title: Portal processes identified parent and child account data during grade request
description: When the parent logs in and requests a child's grades, the web app processes direct identifiers and the explicit parent-child account linkage. This creates an identifying threat because the flow necessarily ties the request to a specific parent and a specific child.
assumptions: The request includes or is associated with authenticated parent account identifiers and a link to the child's account.

title: Grade request reveals sensitive academic information about a specific child to the application
description: The incoming request causes the application to handle a request for the child's grades, which are personal data. Even if the actual grades may be returned on a later flow, this request discloses to the application which child's educational records are being accessed and that the parent seeks that information.
assumptions: Academic grades are treated as personal data and the request identifies the child whose records are sought.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; the retrieved context did not provide a more specific disclosure node.

title: Parent-child linkage is observable from the login and grade request
description: Because the parent account is linked to a child account, the flow enables the application to establish or confirm the relationship between the parent and the specific child. This creates linkability risk beyond processing either account in isolation.
assumptions: The web app can correlate the authenticated parent identity with the child account referenced for grade retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; retrieved context did not include the detailed linkability subtree.

title: Parent may be insufficiently informed about processing of linked child-grade access requests
description: If the portal does not clearly explain what data is processed when a parent requests a child's grades, including use of the parent-child linkage and any logging of access events, the parent may be unaware of the scope of processing on this flow.
assumptions: Transparency notices may be incomplete or not presented in context during login/request actions.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if the interface or privacy notice does not clearly explain this processing; tree node chosen by best judgement.

title: Processing child grades via parent-linked access may lack an appropriate legal basis or policy constraint
description: This flow processes a child's educational data in response to a parent's request. If the portal does not properly enforce jurisdiction-specific rules, custody restrictions, age-related rights, or school policy constraints, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable education/privacy rules may restrict which parents can access which child records and under what conditions.
uncertainty_note: This is a context-dependent compliance threat; exact legal obligations are deployment-specific, and the tree node is selected by best judgement.

title: Exposure of a child's academic record to the wrong parent account
description: If the portal displays grades, teacher feedback, or submission history to an incorrectly linked or authenticated parent account, the flow reveals personal educational data about the child to an unintended recipient.
assumptions: Assumes parent-child account binding or session handling could be incorrect or insufficiently verified before displaying records.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure of content on a Process->ExternalEntity flow; the retrieved context confirms the threat type is applicable but does not provide a more granular node.

title: Parent can infer sensitive traits or circumstances from displayed school records
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may allow the parent to learn or correlate sensitive information about the child, such as learning difficulties, behavioral issues, special educational support, or patterns of absence and performance over time.
assumptions: Assumes the displayed educational records contain enough detail to enable inference beyond the immediately intended purpose of showing academic progress.
uncertainty_note: Linkability/inference boundaries can overlap in educational contexts; this is included because combining multiple displayed record types can enable additional inference.

title: Excessive detail in portal view makes the child identifiable beyond necessity
description: Displaying full submission history, detailed feedback, and grades together may expose more directly identifying or uniquely characterizing information about the child than is necessary for the parent's immediate purpose, especially if shared screens or exported views are used.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may present highly granular records in a single view and that data minimization has not been applied.
uncertainty_note: This is a detectability/identifiability-style concern framed on the visibility of the child through the disclosed dataset; exact subtree may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent may be unaware of the extent and sensitivity of historical educational data displayed
description: The portal may present grades, feedback, and submission history without sufficiently clear contextual information about what period is covered, why each category is shown, or how sensitive teacher comments may be, leading to misunderstanding about the nature and implications of the data disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the UI does not adequately explain the scope or sensitivity of the displayed data.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is included only insofar as this specific display flow may omit transparency cues; confidence is lower than for disclosure threats.

title: Displaying full academic history to the parent may exceed consent, expectation, or legal authorization
description: Showing the child's grades, feedback, and complete submission history to the parent may conflict with applicable consent choices, school policy, custody restrictions, or age-dependent student privacy rights if the portal does not limit disclosure appropriately.
assumptions: Assumes there may be role-, custody-, age-, or policy-based restrictions on what a parent is permitted to see.
uncertainty_note: This is strongly context-dependent on jurisdiction, school policy, and family/legal status, but it is a genuine privacy threat for this flow.

title: Account and relationship data can be tampered with in transit or via insufficient input validation
description: The flow carries high-impact identity and relationship attributes (names, emails, roles, parent-child links). If the web app accepts modified requests without strong integrity protection and server-side validation, an attacker or malicious admin could alter roles or parent-child relationships, causing incorrect identity records and privacy-impacting unauthorized association of students and guardians.
assumptions: Assumes the administrator interacts over a networked channel and the portal exposes account-management functions based on submitted request data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement because the retrieved context provides applicable threat types for ExternalEntity->Process flows but not the detailed threat-tree node list.

title: Administrator may be able to deny creating, changing, or disabling accounts and parent-child links
description: If the portal does not keep durable, attributable audit records for account lifecycle actions and relationship changes, an administrator could later deny having created, modified, or disabled an account or altered a parent-child link. This undermines accountability for privacy-sensitive changes affecting data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes administrative actions are privacy-relevant and should be attributable to an authenticated administrator identity with timestamps and action details.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is an informed estimate; exact node naming may differ in the full LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Administrative account-management requests may disclose personal data to unauthorized parties
description: This flow includes personal data and relationship data: names, emails, roles, and parent-child associations. If the request is sent without adequate transport protection, exposed in URLs, logged excessively, or displayed to unauthorized support/operations staff, the data could be disclosed beyond those with a need to know.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may traverse infrastructure where request contents can be observed or logged unless specifically protected.
uncertainty_note: Node id is selected by best judgement due to limited retrieved tree detail.

title: The portal may be unable to verify that the requester is the authorized school administrator
description: If authentication or authorization for this flow is weak, the process may accept account-management requests from an impersonator or from an administrator lacking the proper scope. This creates privacy risk by enabling unauthorized creation, modification, or disabling of accounts and family relationships.
assumptions: Assumes role-based restrictions should govern which administrator can manage which users and relationships.
uncertainty_note: Chosen node reflects detectability/authentication concerns at the receiving process; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Account and parent-child link changes may be processed without adequate notice, consent, or other legal basis
description: Parent-child relationships and contact/account details are privacy-relevant personal data. If the portal allows administrators to create or modify these links and attributes without ensuring an appropriate legal basis, required notice, parental/guardian authorization, or institutional policy constraints, the processing may violate compliance obligations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable education/privacy rules require a valid basis and governance for changing guardian-student associations and account details.
uncertainty_note: Compliance applicability depends on jurisdiction and school governance model; exact tree node id is best-effort.

title: Integrity loss in stored account and parent-child link records
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links into the account directory. If the write is incorrect, incomplete, or overwritten improperly, the directory may contain inaccurate family-linkage or account data, causing privacy-relevant misassociation of students and parents.
assumptions: DS3 stores authoritative or operationally significant account and relationship data used by other services.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on general LINDDUN integrity threat taxonomy; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Excessive disclosure via persisted parent-child relationship links
description: Writing parent-child relationship links into the account directory creates a persistent repository of sensitive relational data. If the directory is later accessed beyond the intended purpose, these stored links can reveal family relationships and educational associations about data subjects.
assumptions: Parent-child linkage is personal data and DS3 is accessible by multiple components or roles beyond P2.
uncertainty_note: This threat is grounded in the sensitivity and persistence of relationship data; exact disclosure mechanism depends on downstream access controls not shown in the flow.

title: Unawareness of account-directory persistence and reuse
description: Data subjects may be unaware that the grading service writes both account records and parent-child relationship links into the account directory, including how long those records are retained and which other components may use them.
assumptions: Notice, transparency, or just-in-time disclosure about this write operation may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency about this backend write is not adequately communicated; this cannot be fully confirmed from the DFD alone.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing family-link data without proper basis or minimization
description: Persisting account records together with parent-child relationship links in the account directory may exceed what is necessary for grading or related account-management purposes, or may require specific legal basis, retention limits, and access restrictions. If these are not in place, the storage operation may violate privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements include purpose limitation, data minimization, retention control, and lawful-basis constraints.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction, institutional policy, and whether storing relationship links in DS3 is necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Linkability increased by centralizing account and family relationship data
description: By writing account records and parent-child relationship links into the same directory, the system enables records about different individuals to be correlated across contexts. This centralization can make it easier to link student and parent identities and activities.
assumptions: DS3 is used across multiple services or contexts, making cross-context correlation possible.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on how broadly DS3 identifiers and records are reused across the wider system.

title: Excessive disclosure of student records to third-party cloud host
description: The nightly backup/replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external cloud hosting provider. This is a cross-boundary transfer of personal data to a third party, and shipping the full dataset may exceed what is strictly necessary for backup/hosting, creating an avoidable disclosure risk under the data-minimization principle.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a separate controller/processor boundary and receives data in a form accessible for storage/replication; the full dataset is not strictly required in identifiable form for every backup operation.

title: Implicit disclosure through rich backup contents and metadata
description: Even if the transfer is intended for resilience, full backups and hosting replication can reveal more than primary records alone: assignment content, grade histories, directory relationships, timestamps, and account structure may allow the provider to infer student performance, course participation, or special categories indirectly. This creates additional implicit disclosure beyond the primary business purpose.
assumptions: Backups include metadata/history and are retained or processed by the provider in a way that makes such inference possible.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for an implicit/secondary disclosure branch; exact node labeling may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Secondary use of replicated educational data by hosting provider
description: Once full grade records, assignments, and directory data are transferred to the cloud provider, there is a risk that the data could be processed for purposes beyond backup/hosting (for example service analytics, support troubleshooting, or model/service improvement), which would be incompatible with the original educational purpose unless strictly governed.
assumptions: The provider has some operational ability to access or process the replicated data and purpose limitation is not technically or contractually enforced end-to-end.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is best-effort; retrieved context did not include unlinkability tree details.

title: Cross-border or processor transfer may violate data-transfer and minimization obligations
description: Sending full student grade and account data to a third-party cloud host may breach privacy/compliance obligations if the transfer lacks a valid processor arrangement, adequate transfer mechanism, appropriate retention limits, or lawful basis for exporting complete educational records to that provider.
assumptions: Applicable law/policy imposes constraints on processor engagement, international transfers, student-record confidentiality, or data minimization for backups.
uncertainty_note: Compliance applicability depends on jurisdiction and contractual setup.

title: Identifiability of students in replicated backups
description: The backup includes full grade records and account directory data, making individual students directly identifiable to the external provider through names, account identifiers, email addresses, or other directory attributes. Direct identifiability increases privacy risk at the third-party boundary.
assumptions: Backups contain direct identifiers or stable account identifiers rather than being pseudonymized before transfer.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is a best-judgement direct-identifiability node; exact numbering may differ by catalog version.

title: Replicated records enable linking of academic performance and account-directory data
description: Because the transfer bundles grade records, assignments, and account-directory information together, the cloud provider can link multiple facets of a student's activity and identity into a unified profile. This linkability may be greater than necessary for the hosting purpose.
assumptions: The replicated data preserves common identifiers across these datasets.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort; retrieved context did not provide specific linkability node ids.

title: Cross-role linking of grade records across student, parent, and teacher views
description: The grading service reads the same grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. If records or access/session context are keyed or correlated across these audiences, the service can link a student's performance data with parent and teacher identities and interaction patterns beyond what each role strictly needs.
assumptions: P2 assembles or derives role-specific views from common underlying records and may maintain identifiers enabling correlation across roles.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types but not detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Exposure of grade information to unintended recipients through view generation
description: Because P2 reads full grade records to generate multiple audience-specific views, an authorization or filtering mistake could disclose grades, comments, or related educational information from one audience's view into another audience's view, or return more detail than necessary for that role.
assumptions: P2 performs role-based filtering or transformation before rendering views.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node id is approximate; the core risk is information disclosure from insufficient output filtering or access control in the reading/serving process.

title: Overly broad read access enables inference about a student's academic status
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized in some views, reading detailed grade records can allow P2 to infer sensitive facts such as poor performance, special accommodations, missing submissions, or behavioral patterns, and expose those in derived views or metadata.
assumptions: Grade records contain or permit derivation of sensitive educational insights beyond raw scores.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id is approximate; disclosure by inference is the intended classification.

title: Role-specific views may reveal the student's identity unnecessarily
description: When building views for parents and teachers, the service may include direct identifiers or stable pseudonyms for students where aggregate or minimally identifying information would suffice, increasing identifiability of grade data.
assumptions: Some consumers of the generated views do not always require full student identity attributes on every access.
uncertainty_note: Applies if certain views could be less identifying; if every consumer always needs named student records, this threat is weaker.

title: Secondary use of grade records for multiple audiences may exceed original purpose
description: Grade records stored for assessment and recordkeeping are being reused by P2 to build distinct views for students, parents, and teachers. If the system does not enforce purpose limitation and audience-specific minimization, the read operation may support uses broader than the original collection or the data subject's expectations.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and audience-specific data minimization are relevant privacy requirements in this system.
uncertainty_note: This is strongest where the system lacks clearly defined lawful/policy basis for each audience's data access.

title: Insufficient transparency/consent basis for parent and teacher access to grade records
description: The service's retrieval of grade records to construct parent and teacher views may not align with communicated privacy notices, consent choices, or policy constraints, especially where age, guardianship, or educational privacy rules limit who may see which records.
assumptions: Visibility of grade records to parents/teachers may depend on jurisdiction, student age, guardianship status, or institutional policy.
uncertainty_note: Exact applicability depends on governance and legal context; the node id is approximate because the retrieved context did not enumerate detailed Nc subtree ids.
